name: Alec Carruthers
description: Alec Carruthers is an MIT EECS PhD student studying data-efficient learning and foundation models for biological science.
focus: Data-efficient learning · AI for science · Continual learning
photoAlt: Alec Carruthers seated outdoors beneath trees
bio: I’m a first-year PhD student in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at MIT studying continual learning, generative modeling (diffusion, flow matching, flow maps), and data curation methods.
Many moons ago, I was an AI Research Engineer at MIT Lincoln Laboratory, working on biomedical foundation models, meta-learning, and diffusion models for various medical image modalities.
Eons ago, I was a data scientist at Apeel Sciences researching hyperspectral imaging and self-supervised learning for applications in materials science.

I aspire to have my work make tangible impact and some of the application areas I find most beneficial for society include: generative modeling for molecular design (proteins, enzymes, small molecules, etc.), multimodal continual learning across healthcare data for an individual to inform decision making, and accurately representing the impacts of a pertubation on a cell (in silico --> computationally)
